summary_text: Abundant cytoplasmic and membranous expression in respiratory and squamous epithelial cells.
Mainly localized to the plasma membrane. In addition localized to the nucleoli and vesicles.

Respiratory epithelia, superficial squamous epithelial cells, urothelium, subsets of cells in gallbladder and seminal vesicle displayed moderate membranous staining with additional cytoplasmic immunoreactivity in many cases. Remaining normal cells were negative.

Many squamous cell carcinomas, a few urothelial cancers as well as a few basal cell carcinomas displayed moderate cytoplasmic and membranous immunoreactivity. Remaining cancer tissues were generally negative.

Moderate to strong membranous and/or cytoplasmic positivity was displayed in respiratory epithelia, prostate, urothelial cells, seminal vesicle, bile ducts and fallopian tube along with subset of cells in squamous epithelia, salivary gland and renal tubules. Moderate nucleolar staining was showed in neurons. Remaining normal tissues were weakly stained or mostly negative.

Moderate to strong membranous and/or cytoplasmic positivity was observed in most squamous cell carcinomas, prostate, urothelial, thyroid, ovarian, endometrial cancers along with few carcinoids and breast cancers. Remaining cancer tissues were mostly negative.

Moderate to strong membranous positivity was observed in respiratory epithelia, squamous epithelia, salivary ducts, bile ducts, pancreatic ducts, urothelial cells, fallopian tube, glandular cells of breast, epididymis, prostate, cervix, uterine and subset of renal tubules. Remaining normal tissues were negative.

Papillary adenocarcinoma of thyroid, cervical and urothelial cancers along with several  breast, prostate, ovarian, endometrial, lung, skin and pancreatic cancers showed moderate to strong membranous immunoreactivity with additional cytoplasmic staining in few cases. Remaining cancer tissues were negative.
Membranous expression in several tissues, most abundant in gastrointestinal tract.

Cytoplasmic and membranous staining of moderate to strong intensity was observed in most glandular epithelia. Squamous epithelia, cells of the CNS and lymphoid tissues were in general weaker stained or negative.
A majority of adenocarcinomas and some squamous cell carcinomas showed moderate to strong cytoplasmic and membranous immunoreactivity. Remaining cancer tissues were negative.
